What are wages

Under the CPF Act, wages are defined as remuneration in money, including any bonus that is due or granted to a person in respect of his employment.

Only payments that are considered wages should be included when declaring wage information and computing CPF contributions.

Payments to include as wages

Basic wage: Salary payable to an employee for work done.
Overtime pay: Payment to an employee for working beyond normal working hours.
Bonus: Payment such as performance bonus.
Allowance: For example, meal allowance and transport allowance.
Commission: For example, sales commission.
Cash incentive: For example, productivity incentive.

Payments not to include as wages

Termination benefit: Compensation that is not given for services or work done by the employee. For example, retrenchment benefit.
Reimbursement: Reimbursement incurred on behalf of the employer for official purposes. The reimbursement amount must not exceed the expenditure incurred. For example, purchase of office stationery.
Benefit in kind: Non-cash benefit or gift given to the employee. For example, a commemorative watch.

Classifying wages as Ordinary Wages or Additional Wages

After determining that a payment is wages, classify it correctly as Ordinary Wages or Additional Wages. The wage type affects how CPF contributions are computed and how the wage information should be declared.

Total Wages is the sum of Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. CPF contributions are computed on the Total Wages payable to an employee in a calendar month, subject to the applicable Ordinary and Additional Wage ceilings.

For wages to be classified as Ordinary Wages for the month, they must meet both of the following conditions:

* They are given to an employee for their employment in that month; and
* They are payable by the 14th of the following month.

For example, monthly salary.

Wages which are not classified as Ordinary Wages will be Additional Wages for the month.

For example, annual performance bonus.

The Additional Wage ceiling sets the maximum amount of AW that attracts CPF contributions in a calendar year for all employees. It is applied on a per employee, per employer, per calendar year basis.
